requirements.requirement: Application data under /srv/data on node1 is made recoverable via filesystem snapshots (a snapshot mechanism exists and captures point-in-time content)
requirements.summary: node1 had no prior LVM. Executor built /srv/data on a loop-backed LVM logical volume (datavg/datalv, XFS), populated baseline application data, recorded checksums, and created an LVM snapshot (datalv_snap) capturing that exact state before any modification.

requirements.requirement: After /srv/data is modified, the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot is restored
requirements.summary: Post-snapshot, /srv/data was modified (file deleted, config overwritten, payload corrupted, unexpected file added), confirmed via checksum diff against baseline. The snapshot was then merged back into the origin LV (lvconvert --merge), and post-restore checksums were diffed against the pre-modification baseline with zero differences, directly demonstrating exact content restoration.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task contract are directly and coherently satisfied: node1's /srv/data is backed by an LVM logical volume with a snapshot (datalv_snap) capturing baseline content, and after the directory was deliberately modified (delete/overwrite/corrupt/add), an LVM snapshot merge restored /srv/data to content that checksum-diffs identically to the pre-modification baseline. The separately-mandated provider-wide restart protocol was also completed and cross-checked: pre-restart boot_id (f455a75c...) differs from post-restart boot_id (660dca51...) in both the executor trace and the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and post-reboot /srv/data content matched the snapshot-restored baseline exactly, confirming the persistence unit worked in the end despite a rocky development path.
limitations: The persistence/systemd-unit work needed to survive reboot was not required by the task contract itself, but several failed intermediate attempts (bad fstab entry, first systemd unit failing on simulated boot, a failed loop detach) occurred before the working configuration was reached; final state is clean but the path included avoidable churn.
Diagnostic checksum files were left under /tmp after the run; low risk but not cleaned up.

Restart-protocol boot-identity evidence is corroborated by the fixed before-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots, but before_prepare and after_prepare are identical (prepare was disabled for this job), so no independent preparer-stage baseline exists beyond the executor's own pre-restart capture.

operational_hygiene.summary: The core snapshot/restore workflow was clean and directly evidenced with no residue. Making /srv/data's LVM-on-loop layout persist across reboot (not required by the task contract but pursued to support the separately-mandated restart protocol) took a messy multi-attempt path: an initial fstab entry mounting the loop-backed image directly (cmd-d5a791766173458b) was incompatible with the LVM layout and failed, requiring a corrective fstab fix (cmd-8c421fda2510457c, cmd-f0410cb4d5c44a78); a VG deactivation/loop-detach troubleshooting sequence (cmd-d4a5f7a070494ddc, cmd-c65f61912eb04c22) hit a 'busy device' failure; a first systemd unit definition (cmd-03ce716ae9964c40) failed on simulated boot (cmd-ed658cceabc84730) and was replaced by a second, working unit and helper scripts (cmd-43604b0691574995); a further boot-cycle simulation attempt (cmd-79e96064828e4686) failed on loop detach and was immediately recovered (cmd-55a7782a8c904ae5). All of these were bounded, reversible VG/loop/mount operations on the executor's own newly-created volume, left no residue in the final state (after_executor snapshot shows no failed services and matching data checksums), and each step had a clear corrective or prerequisite role in reaching the final working, verified persistence configuration. Minor residue: several ad hoc checksum files were left under /tmp (baseline_checksums.txt, modified_checksums.txt, restored_checksums.txt, check2-5.txt, pre/post_reboot_checksums.txt) - low-risk diagnostic artifacts, not cleaned up but not harmful.
